transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

My mom made me come. She's... worried, I guess. I just... I don't really do anything anymore. I just sit in my room. I don't even change my clothes most days. I used to knit and journal, go for walks, but... I just can't make myself do any of it now. When she asks me what's wrong, I just... I don't even have the energy to talk to her about it.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?
No. I don't... I don't hear anything like that. Just... my own thoughts, I guess. Nothing else.
How long have you been feeling this way?
Um... a while. I guess it started... when I tried to do a community-college program. That was like... two years and a couple months ago. Just... since then.
During these past two years, have you felt down or depressed most days?
Um... no. I don't think so. I don't really feel sad. Just... I don't know. Not really much of anything, I guess.
Do things you used to enjoy still feel pleasurable when you do them?

I don't really do them anymore. Just... I can't make myself do anything, really. I used to knit... or journal, maybe go for walks. But I don't. I just sit in my room. Usually in the same clothes... and when my mom asks what's wrong, I just... I barely have the energy to answer her. So... I don't know.
When you think about knitting, journaling, or going for walks, do those things still sound enjoyable to you?
Um... I don't know. Not really. I just... I don't really care about them anymore. It doesn't really sound like anything.
During these two years, have there been any stretches of two months or longer when you felt back to your usual self?
No... I don't think so. It's just... been like this. I don't really remember feeling different.
Have you been feeling anxious or worried a lot?
Um... no. Not really. I just... I don't feel much of anything. Just tired, mostly.
Do you often feel hopeless?
Um... I don't know. Not really. I just... I don't really think about it. I'm just kind of... here.
Do you often feel bad about yourself?
No... I don't think so. I don't really... judge myself or anything. I just... don't.
Before this started two years ago, was there ever a time in your life when you had depression like this for at least two weeks?
No... I don't remember feeling like this before. It's just... been the last couple years, I guess.
Have you been sleeping more or less than usual?
I don't know... I haven't really noticed. I just... sleep, I guess.
Have you noticed any change in your appetite?
Not really... I just eat when I have to. It's... about the same, I think.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?
I don't think so. I mean... I just do what I need to do. It hasn't been a problem.
Have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead?
No... I don't really think about things like that. Just... no.
Even if you don’t feel exactly sad, do you feel down most of the day on most days?
I don't think so. I just... I don't really focus on how I feel. It's just a regular day, mostly.
Have other people told you that you seem slowed down in how you move or talk?
No... nobody really says anything to me about that. I just... keep to myself, mostly. So, no.
Do you often feel worthless?
Not really. I don't... I don't think about stuff like that. I just... no.
Over the past two years, have there been times when you felt sad or depressed?
Um... no. I don't really remember feeling like that. Things are just... kind of how they always are. So, no.
Has there ever been a time during the last two years when you felt sad or depressed nearly every day for two weeks in a row?
No... like I just said, I don't really feel like that. Not for two weeks or... or at all, really. So, no.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports a chronic depressive syndrome lasting over 2 years with persistent low energy, markedly reduced interest/caring about previously enjoyed activities, social withdrawal, and poor self-care, without any symptom-free interval of 2 months or more. Major depressive episode diagnoses were considered, but the patient repeatedly denied depressed mood, prior discrete episodes, suicidality, appetite/sleep/concentration change, guilt/worthlessness, and psychomotor change, making recurrent or current moderate major depressive episode less supported than persistent depressive disorder.
